note: PASS with a real caveat (canonical wording, order not independently pinned). Instrument is the Satisfaction With Life Scale (SWLS; Diener, Emmons, Larsen & Griffin 1985): the source paper states "The SL scale contains five items presented in seven-point Likert scale format (Diener et al., 1985)", matching the live 5 items sl_1..sl_5 x resp 1-7, and the deposit's SL1..SL5 columns. Step 3b clean -- the deposit's three siblings are OXH (29 items, 1-6), QL (26, 1-5) and PAN (20, 1-5). TEXT is the canonical instrument, not this study's materials: peerj-06-4903-s001.xlsx has bare headers SL1..SL5, no Excel cell comments (the .xlsx contains no comments part at all) and no SPSS variable/value labels, and the article reproduces no SWLS item. Wording, instructions and the seven anchors were transcribed from SWLS_English.doc as distributed on the SWLS's own page (labs.psychology.illinois.edu/~ediener/SWLS.html); the instructions ship as the canonical form's, since neither the paper nor the deposit publishes what this sample was actually told. Nothing was altered: the anchors are listed 7..1 on the form and are simply re-ordered to ascending resp here. MAPPING reconstructed, Step 5b PARTIAL: the paper's Table 2 for the SL scale (n 178, 5 items, M 4.57, SD 1.196, alpha 0.871) reproduces exactly from the live table (178, 4.571, 1.196, 0.871) and SLTOTAL equals the raw sum of SL1..SL5 for 178/178 respondents against 8/178 for the reversed reading -- which pins the anchor direction (1 = Strongly disagree) and confirms all five codes belong to the SL scale stored raw, but distinguishes no SWLS statement from another. Only sl_5 is singled out, by the lowest mean (3.98 vs 4.36-5.00), the largest SD (1.81) and a 10.7% floor against 1.1-2.2% elsewhere -- the expected signature of the counterfactual item -- with sl_4 and sl_5 carrying the weakest item-total correlations (0.641, 0.655 vs 0.727-0.791). Order within {sl_1,sl_2,sl_3} and within {sl_4,sl_5} is not established. RIGHTS: ships, applying the settled `ship` verdict already recorded for the SWLS in instrument_rights_register.csv (2026-09-04, "two pages, two terms") rather than re-deriving it. The page the wording was actually taken from states: "The scale is copyrighted but you are free to use it without permission or charge by all professionals (researchers and practitioners) as long as you give credit to the authors of the scale" (https://labs.psychology.illinois.edu/~ediener/SWLS.html, sha256 5c672e3d7d2312d4b6269d7a51b5403d744c9360d3c84f31f6329d838897b021, re-fetched live 2026-09-08; the linked Documents/SWLS_English.doc, sha256 b53b444d2e6a6efee8fa2b4ab2a805de9af6d2c741d2def5645fa4ea9b2f7b63). Attribution is a condition of credit, not a reserved right -- no fee, permission requirement, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause appears on that page. FLAGGED, NOT RESOLVED: the same rights holder's eddiener.com/scales page says the Diener scales are "permitted for non-commercial purposes only", and the register's SWLS row is marked UNSTABLE with "Escalate before extending"; the register's own Diener/DIENER-NC row nonetheless carves the SWLS out ("the SWLS has a second, permissive page and is NOT blocked"), and SWLS tables shipped as recently as batch_080 on that basis. This table is shipped on the recorded verdict; the escalation the register asks for is still owed by whoever owns that ruling, and if it goes the other way this table and its ~6 live siblings withdraw together. Sibling context: medvedev_2018_oxh and medvedev_2018_pan shipped in batch_098; medvedev_2018_ql is BLOCKED (WHOQOL redistribution bar). Administration was English (NZ university students), so no language/_translated columns.
public_note: The Medvedev (2018) PeerJ deposit labels its life-satisfaction columns only SL1..SL5 and the article reproduces none of the five statements, so the item text shown here is the canonical Satisfaction With Life Scale wording (Diener, Emmons, Larsen & Griffin, 1985) assigned by item number, and the instructions are the canonical form's rather than what this sample was told. The data confirm that all five codes are the SWLS stored unreversed and that resp runs 1 = Strongly disagree .. 7 = Strongly agree -- the paper's published scale statistics (n 178, M 4.57, SD 1.196, alpha 0.871) reproduce exactly from these five items -- but nothing in the source distinguishes one SWLS statement from another, so the order within the scale is inferred from the instrument's printed order rather than stated by the study.

note: Lexical decision megastudy: the IRW `item` code IS the stimulus letter string itself (data/megart_tonković_2021.R does `item = string` on the deposit's own `string` column), so item_text reproduces that string verbatim and no code->text inference exists. resp = stimulus_acc, documented in cda1012_doc_variable-metadata.tab as "Is the participant's response correct or incorrect" with values TRUE;FALSE, so option_text is Correct=1 / Incorrect=0; the live data confirms the direction outright -- 3054 of 5208 items have resp identically 1 and 0 items have resp identically 0, which is only possible if 1=correct. correct_response=1 follows that documented key (twod_rotation_mather2023 precedent for accuracy-scored tables). instructions are the two task sentences from the study's Croatian informed-consent form (cda1012_doc_informed-consent.docx, section 'Postupak istraživanja'), NOT the on-screen E-Prime instructions: those live in cda1012_src_MegaRTChronos_[1-2].es3, whose <Doc> payload is an encrypted E-Prime 3 blob (base64, no zlib/gzip magic) that cannot be read outside E-Prime; the consent text itself says the detailed instructions were presented on the computer, and that sentence is shipped so a reader can see the gap. instructions_translated is this project's own English. No item_text_translated is emitted: the items are single Croatian nouns and Wuggy-generated pseudowords, and about half of them have no meaning to translate -- translating a lexical-decision stimulus would destroy it. Rights: deposit is CC BY 4.0; the stimuli are common nouns from the Croatian Psycholinguistic Database plus generated pseudowords, and no rights-holder restriction on the wording was locatable (nothing in instrument_rights_register.csv), so silence-is-permission applies.
